notes:
T327 — weizigo_showscores GTP command (score-annotated ASCII board). Worker context dump.

WHAT I READ:
- untracked/T327-score-annotated-board.md (the brief)
- src/gtp.zig (existing showboard, weizigo_score, weizigo_estimate, KNOWN_COMMANDS, the runSession dispatch loop; T326 handicap surface as a recent precedent for in-process artifact construction and the side-relative convention)
- src/artifact2.zig (Row type, lookup function, koBits, koNone, encodeKeyByte, keyByteLookup — needed to construct the test artifact and understand the WZO2 Markov key)
- src/rules.zig (pos_from_move, koAfterCapture, MoveError, KO_NONE semantics)
- src/colex.zig (colex_from_pos, Indexer; used in the test to build groups/entries)
- findings/README.md + docs/infra/agents/findings-schema.json (the findings schema)
- findings/T326-gtp-handicap.json (a recent T-ancestor — T326 used the same WZO2 in-process artifact pattern for its test, which I copied and adapted)
- AGENTS.md, docs/infra/delegation/DELEGATEE.md, the managent standing rules

WHAT I CONCLUDED (and on what evidence):
- The brief wants a pure render command on top of the existing WZO2 table, no solver changes. The values printed are table lookups; the engine is already C1-correct on the chainable region and the lookup miss path is the existing bounds2 fallback. The new code is display-only.
- The cell width must be fixed for column alignment. Settled on 4-char cells (3-char content right-aligned + 1 separator) because (a) it accommodates ±16 in 2 digits with sign, (b) it keeps the rightmost content char in the same column whether the cell is L==H, L<H, occupied, illegal, or miss, and (c) it matches the existing showboard's '1 char + 1 space' visual rhythm when both boards are read together.
- L<H cells lose the second digit (sign + leading digit + `~`); the full bracket lives in the footnote, which the brief explicitly OKs ('prefer compact variants ... and expand the marked points to their full [L,H] in a footnote line under the board'). The cell identifies WHICH cells are L<H and the rough magnitude; the footnote has the exact bracket.
- 'silent-unless-asked' is the right default — a per-move auto-print would interleave a multi-line block with Sabaki's GTP console and bury the move reply. The board is a slow-readable artefact; the GTP loop is fast. The user calls weizigo_showscores when they want a fresh look. The brief explicitly allows this if explained.
- The clamped variant (-9 meaning ≤-9) is out of scope — the unclamped form fits the 4x4 range ±16 in 2 digits. The brief says 'the human picks' after seeing samples; the unclamped sample is in the findings and the human can request a clamp variant in a follow-up.

WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH:
- Whether Sabaki (or any specific GUI) wires weizigo_showscores into a visual widget. The brief is silent on this; the GTP command is a general-purpose query a GUI can poll. This is a documentation gap, not a code defect.
- Whether the column alignment reads cleanly in Sabaki's font + tab-stop handling. The output is plain text with fixed-width cells; if Sabaki's font is not monospace, alignment may break. The same caveat applies to the existing showboard. Not in scope for this task.
- A 4x4 mid-game position with a 2-digit L value, an illegal point, AND an L<H point SIMULTANEOUSLY from a real game line. I built the test with a hand-crafted in-memory artifact (T283 pattern) and a position engineered to exhibit all three at once. The real 4x4 v2 artifact also produces all three at the position used in the rendered sample (the 4-move line in the findings notes), so the production code path is exercised by the binary.

WHAT I ASSUMED WITHOUT CHECKING:
- That the existing wzo1 path (Decoded.vb / Decoded.vw arrays, UNDEF sentinel) is the correct shape for the legacy artifact. I did not run the binary against a wzo1 artifact — the T326 task already verified that path doesn't crash, and my lookupChild uses the same shape.
- That the GTP `reply` field for multi-line commands is preceded by a leading newline so the first goban row is not indented by the '= ' response prefix. I matched the existing showboard's pattern (which also starts with \n), so this should be consistent.

WHAT I NOTICED BUT DID NOT ACT ON:
- A pre-existing behavior in the play handler: when a White move is suicide against a Black stone that would otherwise be captured, the engine applies the move AND leaves the opponent stone in place (saw this while constructing test scenarios). The w:D4 / b:D3 example I traced shows the move was accepted with `=` but the capture didn't happen, leaving a 0-liberty White stone adjacent to a 0-liberty Black stone. This is NOT from my changes — the same behavior reproduces from a stashed HEAD build. It is a latent defect in pos_from_move or the play handler, but it's pre-existing and out of scope for T327 (the brief is GTP surface only, no rules change). Recorded as a finding for the next sweep, not a regression of mine.
- A separate issue: the showboard output I traced for the 16-move test had 10 stones where I expected 13, even though all 16 `play` commands returned `=`. Same root cause (the pre-existing capture bug above) — not in scope.
- The 'eyes-clamp' (clamping at ±9) would also need a separate visual style decision (e.g. red color in Sabaki) that the brief doesn't define. Not implemented.

NEXT:
- If the human wants the clamped variant, that's a one-line change in formatShowScores (replace |L|>9 with `9~` or `-9~`) plus a new sample in the findings.
- If the human wants auto-print on play/genmove, the silent-unless-asked wiring would move from the weizigo_showscores command into the play/genmove handler. This was considered and rejected in the brief discussion (see WHY 'SILENT-UNLESS-ASKED' in the findings).
- If the latent capture/suicide defect in the play handler is real, it's a separate task to investigate (not in T327 scope). The T327 code is built on top of the existing move pipeline, so the defect (if it is one) propagates but does not originate in T327.
